{"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "It sounds like you've already finished Step 1 of learning a language ("Do stuff with it").", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "To take your Python knowledge to the next level, I would recommend taking a few steps:", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Read important PEPs. PEP stands for  Python Enhancement Proposal, and is the primary mechanism by which language and library features are officially debated, clarified, and ultimately included or excluded.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "PEP 8 ( http://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/ ) is a good one to start with. Also, look at 318 ( http://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0318/ ). Reading PEPs is a great way to get a concrete handle on the philosophy and thought processes that go into Python language features.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Poke around the Python stdlib itself and read the source. A lot of it is pure-Python, the rest is C. It's a good way to understand what features the language has, what it doesn't, and how you can code idiomatically. The stdlib itself has some good examples of style, and it serves as a good benchmark for Python code.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Patch the stdlib. Just for yourself, just for fun. Add print statements, step through code and see if you can make any optimizations, etc.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Read Doug Hellman's Module of the Week blog ( http://www.doughellmann.com/projects/PyMOTW/ ) . It goes in depth into a lot of different Python modules and is a great way to get a handle on all the corners of the language's libraries.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Hang out in #python on Freenode. There are always a lot of beginners there who need help, and helping others is a great way to improve your own skillset.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "And of course, stay active on Quora and peek around the Python posts here. There are some interesting questions asked and answered here on intermediate and advanced Python, especially on topics like the GIL and the Python interpreter internals. See: 
 ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "How does a Python interpreter work?", "modifiers": {"link": {"type": "question", "qid": 74370, "url": "https://www.quora.com/How-does-a-Python-interpreter-work"}}}, {"text": " 
 ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "What is the GIL (Global Interpreter Lock)?", "modifiers": {"link": {"type": "question", "qid": 1883, "url": "https://www.quora.com/What-is-the-GIL-Global-Interpreter-Lock"}}}, {"text": " 
 ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "How does the Global Interpreter Lock affect performance in multi-threaded Python applications?", "modifiers": {"link": {"type": "question", "qid": 100887, "url": "https://www.quora.com/How-does-the-Global-Interpreter-Lock-affect-performance-in-multi-threaded-Python-applications"}}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "The last and ultimately "best" way in some sense to improve your knowledge of Python is to keep building increasingly non-trivial applications and getting your code reviewed and torn apart by someone more experienced than yourself.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "
Good luck!", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}]}

answer.content: {"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "Leveling from \u201cintermediate\u201d to \u201cadvanced\u201d in Python means expanding depth (language internals, performance, typing), breadth (ecosystem, tooling), and habits (design, testing, collaboration). The following roadmap is practical, task-focused, and ordered so each step compounds previous gains.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Deepen core Python knowledge", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "ordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Data model and special methods: master ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "init", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}, {"text": ", ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "new", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}, {"text": ", ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "repr", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}, {"text": ", ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "str", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}, {"text": ", ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "hash", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}, {"text": ", ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "eq", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}, {"text": ", descriptors, ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "getattr", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}, {"text": "/", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "getattribute", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}, {"text": ". Implement custom containers and immutable types.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Iterators/generators/coroutines: write lazy pipelines, custom iterator classes, use yield from, understand generator.close()/throw(), and generator-based coroutines.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Context managers: implement with ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "enter", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}, {"text": "/", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "exit", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}, {"text": " and contextlib.contextmanager; use ExitStack for composite cleanup.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Metaprogramming: use decorators (preserving signature with functools.wraps), class decorators, and basic metaclasses for domain-specific APIs.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Internals: garbage collection, reference counting vs cyclic GC, name lookup, attribute resolution, import system. Read CPython source snippets for hot paths.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Adopt strong typing and static analysis", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "ordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Type hints: annotate progressively (functions, classes, containers, protocols). Use typing.TypedDict, TypedProtocol, ParamSpec, TypeAlias.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Static checkers: integrate mypy (strict mode) and pyright. Fix type errors rather than silencing them.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Runtime contracts: add runtime checks selectively with icontract or typeguard in tests.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Write robust, maintainable code", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "ordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Testing: unit tests (pytest idioms, fixtures, parametrize), property-based testing (hypothesis), integration tests, and test doubles (mocks). Aim for meaningful coverage, not 100% lines.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "CI/CD: configure GitHub Actions/GitLab CI to run linters, tests, type checks, security scans.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Linting and formatting: enforce black, isort, flake8/ruff rules; use pre-commit hooks.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Documentation: docstrings (Google/NumPy style), Sphinx or MkDocs, publish docs for libraries.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Learn performance tuning and profiling", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "ordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Microbenchmarks: use timeit and perf to measure reliably; avoid naive timings.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Profiling: use cProfile, pyinstrument, scalene, memory_profiler. Identify CPU vs I/O vs GC hotspots.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Optimizations: algorithmic improvements first; then use built-ins, list/dict comprehensions, local variable binding, avoid excessive attribute lookups, use array modules (array, numpy) for numeric work.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Concurrency: choose the right model\u2014asyncio for I/O, multiprocessing for CPU-bound, threads with concurrent.futures for mixed tasks. Understand GIL implications and interprocess communication patterns.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "C extensions and acceleration: use Cython, PyO3 (Rust), Numba, or move hotspots to C/Rust when warranted.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Master advanced libraries and ecosystems", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "ordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Web/backend: FastAPI, Starlette, uvicorn, ASGI patterns; dependency injection and background tasks.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Data: pandas advanced indexing, groupby internals, vectorization; Dask for scale; PyArrow, Parquet; SQLAlchemy core and ORM deeper features.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "ML/AI: PyTorch core concepts (autograd, custom modules), ONNX exporting, model serving (TorchServe, Triton).", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "ordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Clean architecture: separate layers, dependency inversion, hexagonal architecture for services.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "API design: design stable public APIs, semantic versioning, deprecation strategies, and backward compatibility tests.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Patterns: apply appropriate design patterns (factory, strategy, builder) but prefer idiomatic Python solutions (duck typing, first-class functions).", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Observability: structured logging, metrics (Prometheus), tracing (OpenTelemetry), and health checks.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Tooling, workflows, and reproducibility", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "ordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Debugging: pdb, ipdb, rich.traceback, debugging in IDEs (VS Code, PyCharm).", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "REPL and notebooks: mastery of IPython, Jupyter ecosystems, nbdev for literate programming.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Virtual environments, dependency management: pip-tools, poetry, pipx, and reproducible lockfiles.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Containers: Docker best practices for Python images (multi-stage builds, slim base images, non-root user).", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Contribute and learn from real code", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "ordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Read source: study CPython modules, popular libraries (requests, pydantic, fastapi) to see idioms and trade-offs.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Code review: both give and receive reviews. Focus reviews on readability, testing, performance, and API contracts.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Open source: fix bugs, add features, write tests and docs. Small, frequent PRs accelerate learning.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "unordered-list", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Projects: build end-to-end projects (API answer.content: {"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "I suggest peering into the \"functional\" bits of the language and libraries.  Despite claims to the contrary, Python gives you multiple ways to do things.  Look into the built-in map() and filter() functions and their kin.  Play with the functools and itertools libraries.  Understand lambda expressions.  Peer under the hood and discover how you can override what appear to be built-in functions, such as \"==\".  That should keep you busy for a while, but it's just the tip of the iceberg ...", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}]}

originalQuestionIfDifferent.originalQuestionText: {"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "How do I go from a beginner python developer to intermediate then advanced?", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}]}

answer.content: {"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "Thanks for A2A.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Keeping it simple, practice practice and practice.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Being a beginner is easiest, if you have done other language you are already here. Start with online tutorials & videos. Experiment with simplest of problems that uses string manipulation, arithmetic operations and function calls. Personal suggestion: Don\u2019t use IDE (PyCharm, etc..) during this time, I started with Sublime Text and simple code highlighter only. As for now don\u2019t bother with Py2.7, use Py3 it is the future.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "For intermediate, explore python. By explore I mean, play with structural programming and move to OOP. Make a habit of consulting pydoc first (online docs and pydoc terminal command). Implement most used/popular data structure and design patterns, at the same time study which type of problem could that pattern be most useful for. Study how different libraries (simpler ones you used in beginner phase) are developed. Try to improve scripts you wrote during beginner phase using new found skills, make is functional or even implement it with class. Work with multiple files, split you single long scripts in different classes, use your class as libraries. Play with virtualenv. Get yourself acknowledged (just know about these, not necessarily development) with most powerful python libraries (Flask/Django for Web, NumPy for Computational, pandas for Data Manipulation, Keras/ScikitLearn for AI, NLTK for NLP, MatPlotLib for Visualization,\u2026 you got the gist.) Finally, find and solve online programming challenges.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Now advanced for me is specific, ie, where you want to take your python expertise. Overall python pro is too vague and a lot to grasp. For most part, intermediate level will do. If you have made your mind about where your next step lies, may it be Web, Data, AI or stuff, you know enough which you need to learn in deep.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "For example you wish to move toward Web development, you need to have knowledge of web technologies and how they work. Then learn how those are implemented in python or any of its framework. Django and its security vs Flask and its simplicity, what your web app needs more. Jinja templates is another must. Frontend is another beast. One can never be JUST backend developer, you should at least know your way around JS, CSS & HTML. Also get yourself acquainted about different web architecture like MVC.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "On other hand, you choose python for AI and stuff; techs mentioned in above paragraph might be useless for you. Here one have to have extensive knowledge of Stats & Probability. Mathematics is heart of AI. Start getting deep on NumPy, pandas, Scikitlearn,\u2026 Rather than just using libraries, first try to understand it. If you can develop a version of it on your own it helps you to get grasp on underlying calculation processes. Solve problems from kaggle, study others\u2019 solution and identify your weak point. Check for math problems & solutions, code the solution in python (without libraries).", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Last one, Python Guru (just a term I use). They are ones who develop and support python. Derive new libraries, improve/optimize existing codes. To be here, learning or even being advance python dev is just a tip of hidden iceberg inside vast concept of programming, mathematics & computational theories. Anyway we are not talking about this, move on.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "In short, intermediate is hardest to master. By the time you are in upper part of intermediate, you can tackle almost any problem using python. Before stepping to advance libraries on your desired path, I suggest you to learn ins-and-outs of general python convention.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Lastly, \u201cLanguage is just a tool to develop. Data structure and algorithm should be your main concern.\u201d Code can be found anywhere once you know what and how to tackle the problem.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Don\u2019t Just Code, Solve Problem.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}]}
